name: Clustermap
tagline: Kubernetes cluster health at a glance.
summary: Every pod is a tile in a treemap. Size is its footprint, color is its health. Open the app and it reads your kubeconfig, draws the cluster, and keeps it fresh.
features: Five health signals: CPU, memory, restarts, pod status, and warning events.
Group by namespace or by node. Click to zoom in, click a pod for its details.
Read-only. Clustermap never changes your cluster.
notes: CPU and memory need the Metrics Server.
requirements: macOS 15.5 or later and Apple Silicon.

media.alt: Clustermap treemap of a Kubernetes cluster

name: Dashi
tagline: Your personal dashboard.
summary: Drop a folder to see the status and latest updates across your workflows, coaches, tasks, conversations, and opportunities. Find what needs attention at a glance.
features: Compact status cards with automatic refresh.
Filter by source or type, and search by name.
Copy prompts for coaching, running tasks, starting or resuming workflows, resuming conversations, and evaluating opportunities.
Coaches show On track, Due soon, or Overdue against their target cadence.
Local and read-only. No AI or account required.
requirements: macOS 26.5 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Framed
tagline: Resize windows to common aspect ratios from the menu bar.
summary: Framed is a macOS menu bar app for quickly resizing visible windows to common aspect ratios.
features: Lives entirely in the menu bar.
Keeps each window's current width by default, or sizes windows to 50%, 61.8% (golden ratio), or 95% of the screen width.
Groups visible windows by app and applies the selected ratios to every window in the chosen group.
Uses macOS Accessibility APIs, so it needs Accessibility permission in System Settings.
requirements: macOS 26.2 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: GrandReveal
tagline: Reveal.js presentations runner.
summary: Drop a Reveal.js deck folder, or an HTML file such as index.html or demo.html, and present it in a native macOS window.
features: Maintains a 16:9 presentation aspect ratio at the window level.
Minimum content size of 960x540.
requirements: macOS 26.0 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Hai
tagline: A simple and elegant attendance tracking application for macOS.
summary: Take roll call with style.
features: Add attendees with a name and an avatar.
Tap an attendee's card to mark them as called or absent.
Reset all attendees with one click.
Your list is saved on your Mac.
requirements: macOS 26.0 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Jiraiya
tagline: A native macOS companion to Jira.
summary: Jiraiya helps visualize your work, focusing on outcomes and providing a clear overview of epics, stories, and progress across quarters and months.
features: Syncs completed stories from a Jira Cloud project, using your email and an API token.
Groups stories into outcomes you define, matched by keywords in titles and comments.
Drill down from quarters to epics, months, and individual stories.
Read-only. Jiraiya never changes your Jira issues. Stories are stored in a local database.
requirements: macOS 15.5 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Kakashi
tagline: Your command reference, one shortcut away.
summary: Keep task recipes as YAML files in a folder. Search them from the menu bar, fill in shared inputs once, and copy each step, ready to paste into your terminal.
features: Quick search from the menu bar or with Option-Shift-Space.
Arguments are quoted for you. Secret inputs stay hidden and leave the clipboard after 60 seconds.
Local, and it never changes your recipe files. Kakashi never runs a command.
requirements: macOS 14 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Maruko
tagline: Format and move your browser bookmarks.
summary: Maruko is a macOS app that cleans up your Chrome bookmarks. It works with a small companion Chrome extension: Maruko analyzes your bookmarks and previews the cleanup, and the extension applies the change through Chrome's own chrome.bookmarks API. No exporting, no importing, and it works with Chrome running and Sync on, so the cleanup propagates to your other devices too.
features: Removes duplicate bookmarks.
Curates a Recent folder of your most accessed bookmarks from the last 30 days, up to 20.
Previews every change and applies it only after you confirm.
Setup is a one-time pairing with the companion extension.
requirements: macOS 26.0 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Mermaido
tagline: Your very handy MermaidJS diagram visualizer.
summary: Edit Mermaid code and see the diagram render.
features: Pan and zoom, with a dark mode.
Step through a sequence diagram message by message.
notes: Needs an internet connection: Mermaid loads from a CDN.
requirements: macOS 26.0 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Toraku
tagline: Simple time tracking for events.
summary: Toraku loads event schedules from a simple JSON array. Each segment has a title, a duration in minutes, and a type. Speaker and music are optional.
features: Segment types: intro, talk, qa, break, outro.
Schedules may include // comments to temporarily disable segments.
When a segment has a music path, Toraku plays that MP3 with a 2-second fade in and fade out.
requirements: macOS 26.2 or later and Apple Silicon.

name: Queries
tagline: Your queries, together.
summary: Keep reusable PromQL and LogQL queries in a native macOS stack. Refresh them together, follow smooth charts, and inspect logs without building a dashboard.
features: Smooth charts that connect across missing samples.
Shared time ranges, independent refreshes, and copyable query text.
Save, reorder, duplicate, import, and export your collection.
requirements: macOS 27.2 or later and Apple Silicon, with gcx installed and authenticated to your Grafana.

name: BEN
tagline: A notation for the structure of a comedy bit.
summary: BEN is a symbolic system for describing the structural logic, cognitive mechanism, and performer status of a comedy bit.
features: Captures the cognitive gap, structural delivery, performer relationship, and the logic of the twist.
Ignores topic, exact wording, cultural context, and taste.

name: DEN
tagline: A notation for how a demo effect makes an image.
summary: DEN describes how a demo effect generates, transforms, colors, and evolves an image. Chains describe mechanisms, not executable programs, buffer storage, or exact frame timing.
features: Chains pass a result from one operation to the next.
Uses prev for feedback.

name: GUS
tagline: A compact notation for the felt structure of a groove.
summary: GUS captures pulse count, anchor, and modifiers. It does not capture instrumentation, dynamics, exact subdivisions, or exact MIDI or audio placement.
features: Pulse: the number of felt pulses in the cycle, such as P4 or P8.
Anchor: downbeat, upbeat, or backbeat gravity.
Modifiers: plain omissions, syncopated omissions, neighbor hits, and upbeats.

name: HAL
tagline: A notation for harmonic center and motion across a song form.
summary: HAL captures section-level tonal gravity, transitions, and resolution trends. It does not capture bar-level timing, voice leading, exact rhythm, or Roman numeral function.
features: A center-state prefix names a section's harmonic gravity.
Operators inside parentheses describe chord-to-chord movement.

name: MEL
tagline: A notation for melodies as motifs and transformations.
summary: MEL describes melodies as motifs, transformations, and phrase roles. It captures what a melody is doing, not exact performance detail.
features: Captures melodic function, motivic transformations, conversational structure, and scale-degree relationships.
Does not specify absolute pitch, key, exact rhythm, harmony, instrumentation, or articulation.

name: PEN
tagline: A notation for the structure and imagery of a poem.
summary: PEN is a symbolic system for describing the structural logic, rhetorical mechanics, and imagery domains of a poem.
example: S4 M≈ V. R≠ D* T↑
features: Captures stanza form, meter consistency, voice, rhetoric, imagery domains, and tone.
Ignores specific vocabulary and subjective meaning.

name: Skills
tagline: Portable skills for AI agents.
summary: A collection of personal skills that work across Codex, Copilot, Gemini, and Claude Code. Each skill keeps its instructions in a SKILL.md file.
features: Designers for portable workflows, tasks, coaches, conversations, and opportunities, with durable state that survives a change of agent.
Writing skills: clear language, succinct documents, career narratives, and recipes.
Tools for diagrams, macOS icons, flashcards, and task logging hooks.
